about: Formula help: how to read the maths. re is tried on a card's maths with spaces removed and \tfrac made \frac; the first that apply are shown.

symbols.name: A derivative: how fast something changes
symbols.says: Read it "d y by d x". It is **not** a fraction to cancel: it means how much $y$ changes for each bit that $x$ changes, right at that point. On a graph it is the **gradient** (the steepness). With time on the bottom, $\frac{de}{dt}$ is how fast $e$ is changing each second.
symbols.example: if $x$ is distance in metres and $t$ is time in seconds, $\frac{dx}{dt}$ is the speed in metres per second. A speedometer shows a derivative.

symbols.name: A dot over a letter
symbols.says: How fast that quantity changes each second: $\dot{x}$ is the same as $\frac{dx}{dt}$.
symbols.example: $\dot{x}$ for a position is a speed.

symbols.name: A dash after a letter (f dash)
symbols.says: The derivative of a function: its gradient at $x$. $f'(x)$ says the same as $\frac{dy}{dx}$ when $y = f(x)$.
symbols.example: if $f(x) = x^2$ then $f'(x) = 2x$: at $x = 3$ the curve climbs 6 for each 1 across.

symbols.name: An integral: adding up over time (or area)
symbols.says: The long S stands for **sum**. $\int e\,dt$ adds up $e$ over time: each moment's value times a tiny bit of time, all added together. On a graph it is the **area under the curve**. The $dt$ says what you are adding along.
symbols.example: speed × time is distance, so adding up (integrating) the speed over a journey gives how far you went. A small error kept up for a long time adds up to a big integral.

symbols.name: Numbers on an integral sign
symbols.says: Where to start and stop adding: from the bottom number $a$ to the top one $b$.

symbols.name: A capital sigma: add them all up
symbols.says: $\sum$ means add up every one of what follows, usually for each value of a counter written underneath.

symbols.name: A limit
symbols.says: What the expression gets closer and closer to as $h$ shrinks towards 0, even if you can never put $h = 0$ in.
symbols.example: it is how the gradient at a point is defined: the slope of a line through two points as they move together.

symbols.name: Delta: a change in
symbols.says: $\Delta$ (capital delta) in front of a letter means **the change in** it: the later value minus the earlier one. $\Delta t$ is a length of time; $\Delta V$ a change in voltage.
symbols.example: the tank went from 20 °C to 35 °C: $\Delta T = 15$ °C.

symbols.name: e to the power
symbols.says: $e$ here is a fixed number, about 2.718 (as $\pi$ is about 3.142). $e^{x}$ is the curve of natural growth; $e^{-t/\tau}$ is a decay that shrinks by the same share every second. (Careful: in control, a plain $e$ with no power is the **error**.)
symbols.example: a capacitor discharging: $V = V_0 e^{-t/RC}$ falls to about 37% after one time constant.

symbols.name: ln: the natural logarithm
symbols.says: The power you would raise $e$ to, to get $x$. It undoes $e^{x}$: $\ln(e^{x}) = x$.

symbols.name: log: how many tens multiply to make it
symbols.says: $\log_{10} x$ is the power of 10 that gives $x$. It turns multiplying into adding, which is why decibels use it.

symbols.name: sin, cos, tan: angles and ratios
symbols.says: For an angle $\theta$ in a right-angled triangle: $\sin\theta$ = opposite ÷ hypotenuse, $\cos\theta$ = adjacent ÷ hypotenuse, $\tan\theta$ = opposite ÷ adjacent. They also describe anything that goes round or waves (AC, vibration).
symbols.example: $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$: a slope 30° up a ramp 10 m long rises 5 m.

symbols.name: pi
symbols.says: About 3.1416: how many times a circle's diameter goes round its edge.
symbols.example: a circle 10 cm across is $10\pi \approx 31.4$ cm round.

symbols.name: omega (small ω)
symbols.says: Usually a speed of turning or of an oscillation, in radians a second: $\omega = 2\pi f$.

symbols.name: Ohm (capital Ω)
symbols.says: The unit of resistance: volts per amp.
symbols.example: a 1 kΩ resistor passes 1 mA for each volt across it.

symbols.name: theta (θ)
symbols.says: Usually an angle. In control, a **dead time**: how long before a change shows at all.

symbols.name: tau (τ)
symbols.says: A **time constant**: how quickly something settles. After one $\tau$ it has done about 63% of its change; after five, all but 1%.
symbols.example: a tank that takes 10 s to reach 63% of a new temperature has $\tau = 10$ s.

symbols.name: lambda (λ)
symbols.says: Usually a **wavelength**: the distance from one peak of a wave to the next. $v = f\lambda$.

symbols.name: rho (ρ)
symbols.says: Usually **density** (kg per cubic metre), or resistivity.

symbols.name: mu (μ)
symbols.says: As a prefix, **micro**: a millionth ($10^{-6}$), as in µs and µF. As a letter, often friction.

symbols.name: phi (φ)
symbols.says: Usually a **phase angle**: how far one wave is behind another, or a magnetic flux.

symbols.name: Other Greek letters
symbols.says: Just names for quantities, like x and y. Common ones: $\alpha$ (alpha) an angle or a coefficient, $\beta$ (beta) a transistor's gain, $\sigma$ (sigma) a standard deviation or a stress, $\eta$ (eta) an efficiency.

symbols.name: Proportional to
symbols.says: $a \propto b$: if $b$ doubles, $a$ doubles.
symbols.example: the current through a resistor $\propto$ the voltage across it.

symbols.name: Approximately equal
symbols.says: Near enough equal: rounded, or a good estimate.

symbols.name: Less than, greater than
symbols.says: $<$ less than; $>$ greater than; $\le$ less than or equal to; $\ge$ greater than or equal to. The wide end faces the bigger number.

symbols.name: Plus or minus
symbols.says: Two answers, or a range either side.

symbols.name: Not equal
symbols.says: The two sides are not the same.

symbols.name: Infinity
symbols.says: Without end: bigger than any number.
symbols.example: an open circuit has a resistance of (nearly) $\infty$.

symbols.name: Square root
symbols.says: The number that, times itself, makes $x$. It undoes squaring.

symbols.name: Standard form: a number × a power of 10
symbols.says: A short way to write very big or very small numbers. The power says how many places to move the decimal point: right for a plus, left for a minus.

symbols.name: A small raised number: a power
symbols.says: How many of that number are multiplied together. A power of $-1$ means divide: $x^{-1} = \frac{1}{x}$. A power of $\frac{1}{2}$ is a square root.

symbols.name: A small letter below: part of the name
symbols.says: A subscript just tells similar things apart. It is **not** multiplied: $K_p$ reads "K p", the proportional gain; $V_1$ is the first voltage; $t_{acc}$ the time to accelerate.

symbols.name: A fraction line: divide
symbols.says: The top divided by the bottom. Work out the top and the bottom first, then divide.

symbols.name: Times
symbols.says: $\times$ and a raised dot $\cdot$ both mean multiply.

symbols.name: Letters side by side: usually multiply
symbols.says: Two letters (or a number and a letter) written together are usually multiplied: $vt$ is $v \times t$, $IR$ is $I \times R$, and $2d$ is $2 \times d$. Three exceptions: an **abbreviation** is one name ($SP$ is the set-point, $PV$ the process value, not S times P); the $d$ in $\frac{dy}{dx}$ belongs to the derivative; and $dt$ at the end of an integral says what you add up along (time).

symbols.name: A number just before a bracket: multiply
symbols.says: Multiply everything inside the bracket by it: $3(x + 2) = 3x + 6$. (A single letter like $f$ before a bracket can instead be a function: see $f(x)$.)
symbols.example: $2(l + w)$ is the distance round a rectangle.

symbols.name: Divide
symbols.says: $\div$ means divide, the same as a fraction line.

symbols.name: A colon between numbers: a ratio
symbols.says: How the parts compare: $3:1$ means 3 parts of one thing to every 1 part of the other (4 parts in all).
symbols.example: a 3:1 gear ratio: the motor turns 3 times for each turn of the output.

symbols.name: A double arrow: so
symbols.says: The step before leads to the one after: "so" or "which means".

symbols.name: An arrow
symbols.says: "Goes to" or "becomes": in a limit, the value it gets closer to; elsewhere, a step or a change.

symbols.name: Three dots
symbols.says: And so on, in the same pattern.
symbols.example: $1, 2, 3, \dots, 10$ is every whole number from 1 to 10.

symbols.name: Two numbers in brackets: a point
symbols.says: Coordinates: how far across ($x$), then how far up ($y$).

symbols.name: f(x): a rule applied to x
symbols.says: Read "f of x". A function: a rule that turns an input into an output. $f(3)$ means use the rule with 3 put in. It is **not** f times x.

symbols.name: Straight bars: the size
symbols.says: The value without its sign.

symbols.name: A bar over a letter
symbols.says: In statistics, the **mean** (average). In logic, **NOT**.

symbols.name: Degrees
symbols.says: An angle (a full turn is 360°), or a temperature in °C.

symbols.name: Per cent
symbols.says: Out of a hundred: 25% is $\frac{25}{100} = 0.25$.
